TITLE : STOCK MARKET PREDICTION USING AUTOFORMER

Stock price prediction remains a challenging yet critical task in financial markets due to the inherent volatility and complex patterns in time-series data. Traditional statistical models like ARIMA often struggle to capture nonlinear dependencies, while machine learning approaches require robust feature engineering to handle market noise effectively. This project proposes an enhanced stock price prediction system using Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (

) networks, which improve upon conventional LSTMs by processing temporal data in both forward and backward directions. The model incorporates multiple technical indicators—including Relative Strength Index (RSI), Simple Moving Averages (SMA), and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD)—to capture market trends, momentum, and volatility. To address real-world applicability, the system implements a walk-forward validation approach, ensuring robustness against temporal overfitting.

-based stock prediction model has significant practical implications in the financial domain. Its ability to accurately forecast stock prices can aid investors, traders, and financial institutions in making informed decisions for portfolio management, algorithmic trading, and risk assessment. The inclusion of technical indicators like RSI and EMA makes the model suitable for integration into existing technical analysis tools. Its scalability also allows it to be applied across multiple stocks and market environments with minimal adjustments. Looking ahead, the model can be further enhanced by incorporating macroeconomic indicators and real-time news sentiment to improve its predictive power. Future work could also focus on multivariate forecasting, where additional financial variables such as volume or volatility are predicted alongside price. Real-time deployment using live data feeds, integration of explainability tools (e.g., SHAP values), and the development of hybrid models combining
with CNNs or GNNs are promising directions to increase both accuracy and interpretability in real-world applications.
